script.title: Chapter 26: Fire in the Pepper Fields

panels.description: Wide, full page width. Midday in the dry season, seen from the fort wall: parched scrub, low hills, a dark green belt of pepper country and palms to the north. On the far horizon, a thin, uncertain line of grey smoke. Nagoji at the parapet in three-quarter back view, one hand on the warm stone. He is Ananthan Pillai now: Kerala topknot, NO turban, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud; white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, knee breeches, European boots, silver chain of office; NOT a mundu. A Nair sentry beside him (white mundu, crossed leather belt), unconcerned, leaning on his spear.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: At first it looked like nothing more than the usual dry season burn.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: A farmer clearing undergrowth. A careless coal from a cook fire.

panels.description: Narrow strip, same horizon, later. The line has thickened and broken, and now smoke rises in two separate places, far apart. Nagoji has straightened. The sentry has stopped leaning.

The war hall inside the fort. A long, low room with carved wooden pillars and a map table heaped with palm-leaf bundles around a hand-painted cloth map of the canal country (ink lines only, no lettering or labels). Padmini Amma (older now, grey through her coiled black hair, lined face, still upright, simple gold, cotton sari hitched for walking, long walking stick) mid-argument across the table with Ramayyan Dalawa (thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth, stylus in hand). Marthanda Varma (V13 face; cream and gold, bare-headed, his hair in a side knot above his left ear, no turban, no crest, gold necklaces, bare-chested, a spear leaning beside him) on a low platform behind them. Nagoji already in the room, by a pillar at the table's edge (Kerala topknot, NO turban, white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain of office). The one action: in the main doorway a runner bursts in, bare chest slick with sweat, and every head turns to him.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Padmini Amma had come to the fort that morning to argue over grain rates and levy schedules.

copy.speaker: RUNNER
copy.text: Raiders! From the west and the north.

panels.description: The runner down on one knee, panting, one hand on the floor. In the foreground, out of focus, only the foot of a walking stick, stopped mid-tap an inch above the floor. No other figure in frame.

copy.speaker: RUNNER
copy.text: Some with Dutch guns. Some with old house banners.

copy.speaker: RUNNER
copy.text: They strike near Padmini Amma's upper fields.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Close on Padmini, turning slowly toward the runner. The men around her are soft and blurred. She is very calm, and that is worse than shouting.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: They chose my fields. Of course they did.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Old men fight their wars in land they have never walked; young ones set torches where women count vines.

panels.description: Ramayyan, fingers pinching the bridge of his nose, palm leaves spread before him, stylus laid down.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Two fronts. Exactly what Ramayyan had feared.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: The timing is not an accident.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Someone has been counting our drills as carefully as we count their gossip.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The northern column was Kollamkara's, bold with whispers of Dutch backing.

panels.description: Wide. The strip as Nagoji pictures it, an aerial view painted like a map coming alive, no figures and no lettering or labels: dense green walls of pepper vines climbing rough bark support posts on both sides of a narrow path; a canal running alongside with low boats; small shrines of stone and carved wood almost swallowed by foliage on the ridges. Two faint smoke trails converge on it, one from the coast, one from the northern hills.

copy.speaker: VARMA (off)
copy.text: We cannot let them hold that strip. If they do, they have a knife at our throat.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I saw the problem as soon as I pictured the map.

panels.description: Back in the hall. Nagoji at the table, finger on the cloth map where the path narrows (map drawn in ink lines only: canal, path, ridges; no lettering or labels). Ramayyan opposite him.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Our horse cannot move at speed through those vines. The path is too narrow. The canal banks too soft.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Foot.

panels.description: Nagoji shaking his head, eyes still on the map. Varma behind, leaning forward on his platform.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Foot will bleed in every bush. Every tree hides a musket. We will lose men in inches.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You have an alternative?

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Tight on Nagoji, lit from the side. Behind him, through a window slit, the two smudges of smoke on the horizon. He does not look like a man who has had a good idea.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The answer came before I wanted it to.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Burn it.

panels.description: Wide. The whole hall gone still. Padmini's head has snapped toward Nagoji. Ramayyan's stylus has stopped above the leaf. Varma does not move. The runner, still kneeling, looks from face to face.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The word hung in the air like smoke.

copy.speaker: PADMINI (small, soft lettering)
copy.text: Burn it?

panels.description: Nagoji leaning over the map table, tracing a thin zig zag along the canal with one finger (map drawn in ink lines only: canal, path, ridges; no lettering or labels). Quick, as if speed could make it smaller.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Not all. A strip. Narrow. Enough to deprive them of cover along the canal.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Then they must choose. Retreat into the open where our horse can run, or stay and be flanked in smaller patches.

panels.description: Two-shot across the table: Padmini standing with her stick, Nagoji straightening to face her.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: You speak of my vines as if they were scrub.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Today, to them, they are a shield. Tomorrow, if they live, they are coin.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I know what I am asking.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Tight on Padmini's hand on the head of her stick, knuckles tightening. Her face above it, eyes fixed on him.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: You know.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: You do not feel.

panels.description: Varma on his platform, looking between Nagoji and Padmini. His voice is quiet; the room leans in to hear it. He reaches down with his spear and drags its tip slowly along the canal on the cloth map, toward the small drawn fort marks (ink lines only, no lettering or labels).

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: If we do nothing, they will move along that corridor until they reach places where our walls are thin and our men few.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: They will write their own terms in our fields.

panels.description: Padmini turning to face the king.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: If we burn, you carve a wound through my land that will take years to heal.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Pepper is not rice. It does not spring back in one season. You cut into my children and their children.

panels.description: Ramayyan, his stylus lying still on the leaf, looking up at her gently. Small inset in the lower corner: Padmini's eyes, closed.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Amma, if we let them keep that corridor, they carve different wounds.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Through forts. Through houses. Through your own name, when they brag of having used your land to break the king.

panels.description: Full width. Padmini, eyes open now, wet and furious, standing straight and bringing her stick down hard on the floor, the tap that stopped on page 1 finally landing. She faces all three men at once.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Do it.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: But do not pretend you did it to me without my consent.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Let every man who walks that blackened line in years to come know that I allowed it, and that I remember every step you take on it.

panels.description: Nagoji, a single nod. His throat is tight and his jaw is set.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I will ride there myself.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I will not ask another to light the first torch.

panels.description: Wide. A column of riders on a dry red road. Nagoji at the head on Kayal, his bay mare with the ochre red-brown coat of earth after rain. Nagoji: Kerala topknot, NO turban, grey at the temples, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud; long white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, knee breeches, European boots, silver chain of office, talwar at his hip; NOT a mundu. Half a length behind on his left, Ponnan on a smaller, lighter Maravar horse, a head lower: broad-shouldered, loose curly hair uncovered, no topknot, thick moustache, clean chin, red shoulder cloth over a short jacket, white mundu hitched above bare knees, a spear. The white coat leads the column. Behind them, Travancore riders in white mundu with crossed leather belts under a red standard with a silver conch. Ahead, dark greasy columns of smoke; sparks drifting in the air around the horses.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The ride to her upper fields was short and long at once.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Short in distance. Long in what it stretched inside me.

panels.description: Large, most of a tier. From the ridge, looking down: pepper vines in dense ordered lines along both sides of the canal, green fruit clusters hanging like beads; the narrow path running between them like a vein. Raiders (Kollamkara's house men: dark indigo or earth-brown cloth, head cloths, bare-chested, no cross-belts; NOT blue coats, NOT red coats) half hidden in the foliage, musket barrels glinting between leaves, small puffs of musket smoke from the shadows. Low, loaded boats on the canal. The riders reined in along the ridge in the foreground, in silhouette, beside a small shrine almost swallowed by leaves.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The sight below made my stomach knot.

panels.description: Ponnan (loose curly hair uncovered, no topknot, red shoulder cloth over a short jacket, white mundu hitched above bare knees, spear) leaning in from his smaller horse at the shoulder of Nagoji (Kerala topknot, NO turban, long white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain), who is already swinging down from Kayal, the ochre-bay mare.

copy.speaker: PONNAN
copy.text: If we hit them from here, we expose ourselves. They have too many places to hide.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: We do not hit them here.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: We hit their shield.

panels.description: Nagoji on foot at the first row of vines, full figure: Kerala topknot, NO turban, grey at the temples, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud; white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, knee breeches, European boots, silver chain of office, talwar at his hip. Crisp dry leaf litter under his boots. The vine line in front of him is untouched and green; the only smoke is the raiders', far off beyond the canal. A Travancore soldier (white mundu, crossed leather belt) hands him a torch, its head wrapped in oil-soaked cloth. Bleeding faintly into the smoke above him, smoke-textured rather than solid figures, like a stain rather than a clean flashback frame: on one side Padmini's face, grey in her coiled hair, the head of her stick beside it; on the other Revathi's face, grey threading her hair, jasmine in her braid, the tali at her throat.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: You will always choose the king first, Revathi had said. The houses later.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Tight: the torch held to the dry leaves and bark at the base of a support post. The flame touches. Nothing has caught yet. Nagoji's face behind the torch, lit orange, waiting.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: For a heartbeat, nothing happened.

panels.description: One standard tier, full width. The flame has caught. Fire crawls up the post and licks at the lower leaves; sap spits white steam from the stem. Nagoji, full figure, steps back from it, torch still raised, soot already on his white coat (red waistcoat, brass buttons, knee breeches and European boots visible; Kerala topknot, NO turban).

High angle. A zig zag of separate fires along the line, with deliberate gaps between them. Nagoji (white coat, topknot) moving along it, Travancore men (white mundu, crossed leather belts) spreading out on either side of him, setting their torches to post after post.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: A controlled burn, as much as such a thing can be in war.

panels.description: The fire jumping where no one meant it to: leaping a careful gap to catch a fallen branch, black smoke boiling up. Two Travancore men (white mundu, crossed leather belts) flinching back from the sudden heat.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Enough, I hoped, to deny full cover without turning the land into a charcoal scar with no hope.

panels.description: Travancore musketeers (Nair men in white mundu with crossed leather belts and matchlocks; NOT blue coats, NOT red coats) kneeling in a line at the edge of the burn, firing into the smoke. In the gaps they created, raiders show only as black silhouettes against the flame, head cloths and bare shoulders, no cross-belts.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: This was a cruel way to fight.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. One action. In the foreground the wind has shifted, and Nagoji, face streaked black, white coat smeared with soot, hauls one of his own men (a Travancore man in white mundu with a crossed leather belt) back out of the smoke by his shoulder cloth. Behind them, in the grey, raiders show only as coughing, stumbling silhouettes, arms over their faces. No bodies.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I do not pretend there was honour in that moment.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It was ugly and hot and filled with the sounds of men and plants dying together.

panels.description: Wide, late afternoon. The corridor is gone: a blackened stretch of ground through the green, charred posts fallen, earth scorched. On both sides, untouched pepper still stands, leaves fluttering in the hot wind. In the foreground ash, a dropped musket and a scorched raiders' house banner (plain faded green cloth with a simple emblem, no writing). Far off, a few singed survivors limping into neighbouring land, one still wading out of the canal. No bodies.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: We did not pursue far.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The fire had done its work.

panels.description: Wide. Night, the same war hall, lamplit, the map table in the middle. Marthanda Varma (V13 face; cream and gold, bare-headed, his hair in a side knot above his left ear, no turban, no crest, gold necklaces) on his low platform at the far end, watching. Sooty soldiers in white mundu sitting quiet along the walls. In the foreground Nagoji (Kerala topknot, NO turban, grey at the temples, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud; white European-cut coat stained black at the cuffs, red waistcoat, brass buttons, knee breeches, European boots, silver chain of office), lowering a brass cup from his lips with a grimace. In the side doorway behind him, Padmini, without ceremony: soot streaks on her sari, hair plastered to her temples with sweat, stick in hand. Every head in the hall is turning toward her.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: That night the smell of smoke clung to everything. Even the water tasted of it.

panels.description: Padmini standing in the centre of the room by the map table, looking straight at Nagoji. Her voice is flat, and her face is flatter. Varma a lamplit shape on his platform behind her.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: You did what you said you would. You burned a strip. Not all. Enough.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: I rode there. I walked the black line. It runs like a mark across my land.

panels.description: Two-shot across the map table: Padmini unmoving, Nagoji answering her.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: For years, men will ask what happened there. I will tell them. They will ask why. I will tell them that too.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: We stopped them. They will not use your vines as cover again.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Nagoji, close. She has not answered him, and he has heard how thin his answer was. He does not look away.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: When the raiders burned your lower fields years ago, you called it an act of cowardice.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Today, I did it with a torch in my own hand. I do not know which ash is heavier.

panels.description: Padmini, eyes hard and unblinking. She rubs a smear of soot from her sari between finger and thumb and lets it fall onto the cloth map, onto the canal where Nagoji traced the strip on page 3 (ink lines only, no lettering or labels).

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: They burned to destroy. You burned to save.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: But ash tastes the same in my mouth, Ananthan. Do not expect me to distinguish the flavour.

copy.speaker: PADMINI (after a breath, a separate balloon)
copy.text: I do not say you were wrong.

panels.description: Reverse angle, over Padmini's shoulder onto Nagoji's face as he takes it. Her voice drops; this is harder for her than the anger.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: If I thought there had been another way, I would be screaming now, not speaking.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: But do not expect me to thank you. There are wounds that are necessary and wounds that are kind. This was the first, not the second.

panels.description: Varma on his platform, face unreadable. Padmini half-turned toward him, leaning on her stick.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You have my word that the state will help replant.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Your word does not make plants grow faster.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: But perhaps it will keep some of my boys from having to sell their swords to men like Kollamkara when the hunger comes.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Padmini at the doorway with her back to the hall, paused, not looking round. Nagoji small in the lamplight behind her.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: You have chosen your side firmly now, Pillai.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: When Dutch, Mysore or your own hills come in force, you will be in front of the king's fort. You will not be standing on my verandah.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: I will remember that.

panels.description: Wide. The fort wall at evening, a few days later. Far off, the blackened strip still visible as a dark line across the green. Nagoji alone at the parapet (Kerala topknot, NO turban, grey at the temples, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud; white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, knee breeches, European boots, silver chain of office; NOT a mundu). Revathi Bayi (a little younger than Nagoji; deep indigo sari with gold, jasmine in her braid, grey threading her hair, tali at her throat, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets, sandalwood line at the hairline) coming along the wall walk toward him.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Revathi's anger arrived a few evenings later, as I had known it would.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You carved your own mark into this land.

panels.description: Nagoji turning to her. She has not stopped walking.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: We carved it together. The king, Ramayyan, Padmini. I merely held the first torch.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Men like you always say that. You hide behind councils and shared decisions when the fire is yours.

panels.description: Revathi leaning on the parapet beside Nagoji, staring north at the strip. Neither looks at the other.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: If a Dutchman had done what you did, you would have called him monster.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Because you did it for a king you respect, you call it necessity.

panels.description: Small panel. Nagoji, turned toward her profile.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You think there was another choice?

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Revathi still facing the horizon after a long silence, the last light on her face. Nagoji at the edge of frame, watching her.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: No.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: That is what angers me most. Sometimes, the only choices left are between a slow death and a quick burn.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You chose well for the kingdom. Badly for the house. As I knew you would.

panels.description: Revathi straightening from the parapet and facing him fully.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: This does not make you evil. It makes you dangerous.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: To love you, as I do, is to love a man whose first instinct is to save the larger pattern, not the smaller square.

panels.description: Two-shot, Revathi and Nagoji. Her gaze flicks toward the blackened strip, then back to him.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You once asked only for a corner of my house and a sliver of my heart. Today you carved a wound across my land instead.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You knew that before we stood before the goddess.

panels.description: Revathi stepping away from the parapet, answering over her shoulder without stopping. Nagoji stays where he is.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Of course. I married you with my eyes open.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: I knew there would be days when you stood on the wall beside the king instead of on my verandah. I did not expect to like it when those days came.

panels.description: Seen past Nagoji's shoulder at the parapet: Revathi, a few paces off along the wall walk, turns back halfway, her face in the last light, one hand at the tali.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: We will work together when it suits the land. We will stand in the same halls. We will share this house in name and in law.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: But do not ask me to pretend this scar is not also your work.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Revathi walking away along the wall walk, her back straight, already small. Nagoji alone and small at the parapet, the evening sky reddening over the walls.

Wide, long lens, sunset. No figures. The burned strip across the green: scorched posts standing as jagged black silhouettes against a red sky, the dark vein of ash running between untouched pepper on both sides.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The fire in the pepper fields had done more than deny cover to raiders.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It had burned away the illusion that love could soften the choices ahead.

panels.description: A canal bank at dusk. Bales of cloth stacked by a moored boat. Ibrahim Marakkar (a stocky, broad-chested coastal Muslim broker; short coat over a vest with bulging pockets; scar from his LEFT ear to the jaw) in three-quarter view showing his anatomical left side, the scar clearly visible, talking quietly with a man seen from behind, in shadow.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Later, when Ramayyan sifted rumours, Ibrahim Marakkar's name floated more than once to the surface.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Whether he had helped Kollamkara reach Dutch guns or had nudged those same whispers toward the fort first was never entirely clear.

panels.description: The war hall by day. Ramayyan (thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth) at his palm leaves, not looking up, stylus moving. Nagoji standing across the table (Kerala topknot, NO turban, grey at the temples, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud; white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, knee breeches, European boots, silver chain of office; NOT a mundu).

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I asked Ramayyan about it once, months after the ash had cooled.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Some men are most useful when both sides believe they are theirs.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Do not trouble yourself with his accounts. I keep them for him.

panels.description: Two-shot across the table. Nagoji leaning in. Ramayyan still does not look up.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And if he betrayed us?

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Then I would know. And he would know that I know. That is usually enough.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Tight on Ramayyan's hand turning a palm leaf, stylus already moving to the next line. A small brass dish of dried black peppercorns weighs down the stack of finished leaves.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Men like Ibrahim rarely walked in straight lines.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Perhaps that was the only way to survive on a coast where every power wanted the same pepper.

args.prompt:
V15 graphic novel panel page-01-panel-01 for chapter 26. Drawn in the book's inked graphic-novel style: clean ink line and painted colour, never photorealistic. Place: Travancore fort wall above the dry country.

Wide, full page width. Midday in the dry season, seen from the fort wall: parched scrub, low hills, a dark green belt of pepper country and palms to the north. On the far horizon, a thin, uncertain line of grey smoke. Nagoji at the parapet in three-quarter back view, one hand on the warm stone. He is Ananthan Pillai now: Kerala topknot, NO turban, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud; white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, knee breeches, European boots, silver chain of office; NOT a mundu. A Nair sentry beside him (white mundu, crossed leather belt), unconcerned, leaning on his spear.

FRAME SHAPE: a wide horizontal strip, about 3 to 1 (width to height), filling the whole width; keep faces and the key action inside the middle half of the height.

PEOPLE IN THIS PANEL: Nagoji. Draw each named person once, with no doubles.

LOOKS (face, build, hair, facial hair, scars, marks and ear ornament always follow these lines; footwear, sleeves, headwear, props in hand and pose follow the panel description above wherever it is more specific):
Nagoji: Constant identity: strong cheekbones, straight nose, thick curled moustache, CLEAN-SHAVEN CHIN, long curly black hair, small gold ear stud, lean cavalryman build. No forehead marks, no sacred thread, no royal jewellery. No facial scar.; in uniform: white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, plain brass buttons, knee breeches, buckled European riding boots, the silver chain of office worn over the coat, Kerala topknot, no hat, no turban, first grey at the temples; the brand and the long white forearm scar on the inner LEFT forearm above the wrist. At Padmini's funeral in ch27 he is bare-chested in a plain white mundu as the script describes.

REFERENCE SHEETS: 1 attached image(s), in this order: 1) Nagoji. They are character model sheets: use them only for faces, build, hair and costume. Ignore everything else on them: backgrounds, scenery, insets, labels, extra poses and props. For Nagoji take only the face and build from the sheet; his costume comes from the text. The hilltop fort, stone cell and fort wall behind the figures on the Nagoji sheet are not part of this panel. His ear ornament is a tiny flush gold stud on the lobe, not the hanging drop drawn on the sheet.

ART RULES:
- 1740s dress, arms, objects.
- No blood or gore; stage aftermath.
- Clay or brass oil lamps; open wicks.
- Non-Maratha raiders' and rivals' banners are plain cloth.

LETTERING: the letterer adds it afterwards, so draw none of it. This panel will carry exactly 2 lettering area(s): a caption (medium); a caption (medium). Leave clear, low-detail space: Keep the pale sky above the far hills clear for two captions, with the thin smoke line still visible beneath them. Keep faces, hands and important action outside that space. Draw NO balloons, caption boxes, panel borders or a border line around the picture, and no written characters, numerals, pseudo-writing, logos or watermark anywhere, including on banners, flags, cloth, walls and documents. Any balloon, caption or letterer wording in the description means space only, never painted lettering.
